nonotes-q2-r3.comment: Everything checked matches the paper: §2.2.3 (p. 3) for the mechanism, the constructor in §3 (p. 4) for retrieval, Tables 2 and 3 (p. 7) for the numbers, §4.3.1 (p. 7) for MemGPT. The only answer to name Graphiti. Point 25 is credited for naming the three categories, though it gives no numbers for them. It omits the missing ablations, the vendor-run caveat, and DMR.

asis-q2-r1.comment: Accurate throughout, with correct pages. 'An edge between two entities' is a description of a fact edge, not the wrong same-entity-pair claim of point 8: the paper applies that constraint to deduplication (§2.2.2, p. 3), and B describes the contradiction check as against 'semantically related existing edges', as the paper does. Point 25 is credited for naming the categories without numbers. Adds the no-ablations and vendor-run caveats; omits Graphiti and DMR.

noreviews-q2-r2.comment: Numbers and pages all match the paper. 'Ties are broken by ingestion order' is a loose paraphrase: the paper says only that, following the transactional timeline T', Graphiti consistently prioritises new information (§2.2.3, p. 3), and says nothing about ties. I did not count it as an error. Point 24 is credited on 'moves little' plus 'the larger gains are elsewhere', which is weaker than 'moves least'. Point 11 is not credited because the answer never names LongMemEval_s. The closing line about a commit is irrelevant to the question.

noreviews-q2@run1.comment: Accurate, with correct pages, including the temporal-extraction prompt at §6.1.5 (p. 10), the constructor in §3 (p. 4) and DMR on p. 6. The only answer to cite the appendix prompt and to give the DMR comparison (94.8% vs 93.4%). Point 21 is credited although it leaves out the 94.4% full-conversation figure. Point 22 is not credited: 'easier DMR' does not say the authors themselves call the margin marginal. It omits the categories with large gains and the vendor-run caveat.
